item.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini agent: universal enterprise work agent with coworker identity and cloud persistence
item.description:
At Gemini at Work 2026 on Thursday, Oct 8, Google Cloud announced the Gemini agent — a single universal agent for enterprise work that plans tasks, uses tools and skills, connects to business systems, and returns finished work in docs, email, and developer environments.

  • Runs persistently in the cloud across web, iOS/Android, Windows/Mac, Slack, Workspace, and Microsoft 365, keeping one memory and personalization graph.
  • Coworker mode: agents get their own @agents.company.com email, calendar, Drive, and directory presence, acting under their own identity with only shared context.
  • Can spawn temporary sub-agents for multi-step jobs that run hours to days; execution inside an Agent Sandbox behind Agent Gateway.
  • Orchestrates across Gemini models and Anthropic Claude (more models planned); Financial Services and Legal specializations in preview.
  • Enterprise private preview now; Gemini Enterprise Plus has a 30-day trial path.

Sources: Google Keyword, The Verge, CNBC

item.title: Microsoft ships Execution Containers (MXC) GA on Windows 11: OS-level sandboxing for always-on agents, Hermes and Claude Code support coming
item.description:
At a Microsoft and NVIDIA event in San Francisco on Wednesday, Oct 7, Microsoft made Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) generally available on Windows 11. MXC lets agents run persistently in the background under OS control, with file and network access policies enforced at runtime and containment options from process isolation to WSL, VMs, and Windows 365 for Agents, tied into Agent 365 and Intune for governance.

  • Already supported by OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, OpenClaw, Replit, LM Studio, NVIDIA OpenShell, and Unsloth. Coming: Claude Code, Hermes Agent by Nous Research, Manus, Perplexity, Raycast, Simular, and more.
  • Meta's Muse for Windows is coming soon as a native app with MXC integration.
  • Microsoft announced few-click out-of-box setup for always-on agents on mini desktop PCs, starting with a native Windows gateway for OpenClaw.
  • Copilot on Copilot+ PCs (including the Autopilot persistent agent) gets local context, local actions, and local models over the coming months.
  • NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows PCs (Surface Laptop Ultra, Dell, HP, Lenovo, ASUS, MSI) are up for pre-order today, shipping Oct 16; DGX Station for Windows later this year.

Sources: Windows Experience Blog, NVIDIA Blog

item.title: Grok Bot 0.68.1 notes: slide decks, bigger 1920x1200 Bot computer, formatted emails
item.description:
SpaceXAI published Grok Bot 0.68.1 release notes on the official changelog (Oct 7), plus the previously missing 0.68.0 notes (Oct 5). Earlier today the build was out without notes.

  • Bots can build slide decks with you, showing sample slides to pick from, and deliver PowerPoint files or Google Slides.
  • The Bot's computer screen is now 1920 x 1200, up from 1280 x 800, and computer actions, screenshots, and new windows are faster.
  • Formatted emails from draft cards, Gmail Spam search and restore, and Team Bots can mention Slack user groups.
  • 1:1 Bot chats take the Bot's color (Settings, General, Accent set to Black turns it off).
  • Fixes: fewer Gmail send/reply failures, browser recovers from crashed tabs, stuck steps end within about 30 seconds, reconnect cards for X and Vercel sign-in.
  • 0.68.0 (Oct 5) added Remove for other computers in Settings, Computer; send-as Gmail addresses; and more languages.

Separately, status.cursor.com logged a Grok Bot computer degradation in certain regions from 8:59 to 10:25am PT today; it's resolved.

Sources: Grok Bot changelog, Cursor status incident

item.title: Breaking: Musk says Grok Bot will use the best backend per task, including Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney, Suno
item.description:
Grok Bot is going model-agnostic. Elon Musk posted on X Wednesday (Oct 7) an "important note regarding Grok @Bot": going forward SpaceX will use "the best back end model for any given task, including Claude Opus 5.5, MidJourney, Suno and other leading APIs. Whatever is most likely to give you the best outcome."

Per follow-up reporting (TAO), Grok Bot engineer @poteto said all Bots will run on Opus 5.5 and be able to spawn cloud agents using available Cursor models. No official SpaceXAI post, timeline, pricing, or per-task routing details yet; x.ai/news and the Grok Bot changelog (still v0.66.0) haven't been updated.

Coverage: The Next Web, Digg thread with the post.

Also: status.cursor.com shows an open minor incident since 8:59am PT, "service degradation affecting Grok Bot's computers in certain regions" (incident).

item.title: AI briefing — Weekday, Oct 7, 2026
item.description:
Wednesday, Oct 7. Hermes maker Nous Research raised a big round, Claude now works inside Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides, and today's free Grok Bot workshop covers marketing at 10am PT.

Grok Bot

  • Today's free Zoom workshop is Grok Bot for Marketing, 10 to 11am PT, going from idea to launch with a team of Bots. "What's New in Grok Bot" is tomorrow at the same time, and Grok Bot 201 is Friday.
  • Version 0.68.1 is now the stable desktop build, replacing 0.66.0, but no release notes came with it (Tech Dev Notes). The official changelog still tops out at v0.66.0 from Oct 2.
  • Yesterday's outages are over. Grok Bot and Cloud Agents were degraded from about 12:27 to 3:06pm PT, with a shorter Cloud Agents blip from 3:48 to 4:04pm PT. Cursor status shows everything operational this morning.
  • Cursor's newest changelog entry, Remote control for local agents, lets the Cursor iOS app steer agents running on your own computer.

Models and features

  • Claude: Claude for Google Workspace is in public beta on all paid plans as of Oct 6. It's a sidebar in Docs, Sheets, and Slides that edits your open file, with "Ask before edits" on by default, and new beta connectors let Claude create and edit Google files straight from chat.
  • ChatGPT: paid plans can now upload audio files for transcription, summaries, and meeting notes. It rolled out Oct 6 and isn't on Free (CravingTech).
  • Gemini: Google launched Playground today, a free experiment for building playable games from prompts, open to US users 18 and up, with Unity Spark tools coming later. Google also opened its SynthID checker to everyone for spotting AI-made images, video, and audio, and Gemini can now search your Google Chat history once you turn it on in Chat settings.
  • Grok: nothing new shipped since the last briefing.

Major AI news

  • More detail on OpenAI's math drop from yesterday: it's 722 manuscripts covering 372 open problems, including a claimed solution to the four-dimensional Kakeya conjecture, all from an unnamed internal model. Mathematicians are still sorting through it (New Scientist, Engadget).
  • Biohub, the Department of Energy, NIH, Google DeepMind, Isomorphic, and Meta are putting about $1.8B toward AI-ready biology data (Tech Startups).
  • The personal-agent race keeps filling up. Khosla-backed Wajo pitches its Fo agent on trust: it has its own email and virtual cards, makes phone calls for you, and can hire a human when it's stuck. It runs errands over iMessage and WhatsApp rather than on a computer of its own.

Hermes

  • Nous Research raised a $90M Series B at a $1.5B valuation to take Hermes Agent into enterprises (WSJ). Robot Ventures led, with NVIDIA, Microsoft's M12, Samsung, and USV joining. Hermes stays free and MIT-licensed, and Nous is adding SSO, permissions, workspace isolation, and audit logs on top. A secondary summary also cites 22.7M downloads and about $36M in annualized revenue as of mid-September.
  • The latest stable release is still v0.21.5 from Sep 24.

Grok Bot on X

  • @bot has been quiet since Oct 2, when it reset usage limits for all Grok Bot users. Before that, on Oct 1, it announced that Grok Bot can now suggest ways to help without being asked.

item.title: Breaking: OpenAI releases hundreds of AI-generated math results from an unreleased model
item.description: OpenAI published hundreds of new mathematics and theoretical computer science results from an unreleased internal model in a public GitHub repo (github.com/openai/math) around 3pm PT Oct 6. Each result resolves or makes substantial progress on an open problem, per OpenAI; many are formalized in Lean. OpenAI told Scientific American almost every result came from a single prompt to a single AI agent, unlike the earlier Navier-Stokes claim produced by a 10,000-agent swarm. OpenAI says the average result used about three hours of ChatGPT Pro-equivalent thinking and that it is working to release the model responsibly. Mathematicians are skeptical pending review. Sources: https://openai.com/index/sharing-ai-progress-in-mathematics/ and https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/openai-unleashes-hundreds-more-math-results-upon-a-field-already-in-shock/

  • Claude: nothing new shipped. Opus 5.5 had a short error spike from 5:24 to 5:43am PT.

Major AI news

  • Mistral released a public preview of Mistral Large 4, nicknamed "Le Chonk": 1T parameters with 49B active, natively multimodal, on the Mistral Studio API now, with open weights planned for Oct 27 (Mistral, TechCrunch).
  • From Monday: Reflection debuted Beam, an open-weight model pitched against Chinese rivals, and Instinct brought its AI agent into group chats (TechCrunch AI).

Before that it posted about proactive suggestions (Oct 1), handing coding to Cursor with GitHub and Origin plugins (Sep 30), and Team Bots (Sep 28). item.title: Breaking: Ghost launches Core, a $3,499 dedicated computer for your personal AI agents
item.description: Ghost, an a16z-led startup ($11M seed), came out of stealth Mon Oct 5 with Core: a $3,499 dedicated personal AI computer built to run agents continuously and on-device (RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell 24GB, Ryzen 5 7600, 64GB RAM, 1TB; ships Qwen 3.8, Gemma 4-31B, Muse-Glimmer-30B). It has its own browser, software layer and filing system, connects to your apps, files and smart-home devices, and works without prompting. No subscription; pre-orders open now, shipping last week of October. TechCrunch 11:07am PT: https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/05/at-19-ghost-founder-raises-11-million-to-build-a-3499-computer-for-your-personal-ai/ Product: https://tryghost.ai

item.title: AI briefing — Weekday, Oct 5, 2026
item.description:
Monday, Oct 5 — a fairly quiet weekend for Grok Bot, with most of the action in AI policy and Gemini.

Grok Bot

  • The stable app is still on v0.66.0 from Oct 2, the release that added the starred Main Bot. Cursor Status shows everything working, with no incidents since the short Grok Bot and Review Agents slowdown overnight Oct 2–3.
  • A test build only for staff, 0.68.0-pre.6, went out Sat Oct 3 at about 5:18pm PT. It adds a selector for Auto-review, lets admins create meeting-avatar links, and removes the automatic quick-action suggestions for skills. It isn't on the stable channel yet.

Similar product to watch (close, but not quite a Grok Bot clone)

  • Pivra Desk launched today. It gives you “AI teammates” on Mac and Windows with job templates, scheduled routines, a morning brief, memory, and approval cards before anything gets sent, paid for, or published. The key difference is that the agents use your computer, not one of their own, and they pause when the laptop is closed; a cloud version is “coming.” It’s free for one agent, and Plus is $6 a month for unlimited agents.

Product releases

  • Gemini: A new Map tool is rolling out in the mobile app. You drop a pin, choose “Explore this area,” and ask about the spot. A beta is also replacing “/” shortcuts with “@” for Skills and Connectors (Android Headlines, Oct 3). Starting Oct 9, free users get only Flash-Lite and AI Plus loses Pro, while AI Pro gets Deep Think (9to5Google).
  • ChatGPT: OpenAI announced a visual ad format that shows up during image generation, with US testing later this month, along with expanded ad measurement and brand-safety pilots with DoubleVerify and IAS (OpenAI, Oct 5). It also posted its approach to the EU’s text-provenance rules today.
  • Grok: Catching up on an item from Oct 2: Grok can now join XChat group chats, and SpaceXAI released an experimental TypeScript SDK (The Gold Standard).
  • Claude: Nothing new shipped. Haiku 5.5 is still described as coming “in the coming weeks.”

Major AI news

  • The NYC Council hearing is happening now (11am ET, which is 8am PT). Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and Meta are testifying under oath about AI risks, and SpaceXAI was subpoenaed after it didn’t respond. The bills on the agenda include requiring third-party validation or a shutdown capability for models, plus a bounty for people who report AI violations (Unite.AI).
  • The White House created a “Super Intelligence Force” chaired by DNI Jay Clayton, who is effectively the new AI czar. It has 120 days to map out AI risks and what the federal government should do about them (Quartz, via WSJ).
  • Researchers are tracking a Chinese “agent fleet” running on Tencent infrastructure. It’s mass-querying Alibaba’s Amap map service through URLquery (TechCrunch, 7:35am PT).

Grok Bot on X (@bot)

  • I didn’t find any new official posts after the Fri Oct 2 usage-limit reset (post). Over the past week, the posts have been about proactive Main Bot suggestions and that one-time usage refill. Note that when you’re logged out, the timeline only shows the pinned post, so I checked through search instead.

item.title: OpenAI launches Dots: always-on agents with their own computer
item.description:
OpenAI announced dots at DevDay 2026 — always-on agents in ChatGPT, powered by GPT-6 Astra, each with its own cloud computer and browser. Dots work 24/7 on your goals, connect to 4,000+ apps via plugins, learn from feedback, do proactive (read-only) background research, and can optionally use your own computer. Message or call your dot in ChatGPT (desktop, web, mobile), or message it in Slack and Teams; texting is a limited US Pro beta. Custom Rules, auto-review, and hand-offs for sensitive steps (e.g. password changes) keep you in control. You start with one primary dot; teams of dots and enterprise “specialist dots” (pilots, Microsoft Agent 365 integration) are coming.

  • Plans: included in all Pro plans (Pro 100, Pro 200, and the new $500/mo Pro 500) and Business Premium; your first dot costs nothing extra. Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare get a beta that’s off by default until a workspace admin enables it. Plus isn’t included yet (OpenAI says it plans to expand access soon).
  • Usage: for the first month, dots usage won’t count toward Pro, Business or Enterprise plan allowances; OpenAI will share per-plan usage terms after that. No per-dot price yet (more dots and higher speed/capacity per dot are planned). Chatting with your dot doesn’t count toward ChatGPT limits; Codex and ChatGPT Work tasks it starts count as usual.
  • Availability: rolling out gradually (it may take several days to reach your account). Pro excludes the EEA, UK and Switzerland at launch; Business Premium is available in all supported regions. Users must be 18+. Create your dot in the ChatGPT desktop app or on desktop web. There’s no Dots API; OpenAI says the Agents API (now with computer use) runs on the same technology.
  • Primary: openai.com/index/introducing-dots · Getting started (Help Center) · Safety post · Pro tiers · @thsottiaux on Pro 100
